usage: 사돈 = the parents of your son- or daughter-in-law (both families call each other 사돈).

examples.en: I'm meeting my in-laws next week.
I met my son's in-laws for the first time at his wedding.
I'm going to have lunch with my child's in-laws tomorrow.
My child's in-laws live near our house.

explain: 사돈을 직접 부를 때는 ‘사돈어른’이라고 많이 해요. 아주 정중한 말이에요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 사돈의 팔촌 정도로 먼 친척이에요.
자기도 늦으면서 사돈 남 말 하네.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구어, 자기 잘못은 모르고 남을 탓할 때
phrases.nuance_en: casual: said when someone blames others without noticing their own fault

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: This is our in-law (the parent of our child's spouse).
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: When you speak to your 사돈 directly, people often say 사돈어른. It is a very polite form.

usage: 손주 = grandchild (any). 손자 = grandson, 손녀 = granddaughter.

examples.en: This is a photo of my grandchild.
Every weekend I go to the park with my grandchild.
I bought a toy for my grandchild's birthday.
Our grandchild is five years old.

explain: 아들의 아이는 ‘친손주’, 딸의 아이는 ‘외손주’라고 해요. 둘 다 그냥 ‘손주’라고 해도 돼요.

dict_examples.ko: 요즘 손주들 보는 재미에 푹 빠졌다.
dict_examples.en: These days I'm completely absorbed in the joy of watching my grandchildren.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: A son's child is a 친손주 and a daughter's child is a 외손주. You can just say 손주 for both.

examples.en: I'm a fan of that singer.
I'm going to a fan signing event.
My younger brother is a baseball fan.
The fans are waiting in front of the concert hall.
I made a lot of friends in the fan café.

explain: 팬이 여러 명이면 ‘팬들’이에요. 팬들의 모임이나 문화는 ‘팬덤’이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 드라마 한 편을 보고 그 배우한테 완전히 입덕했어요.
phrases.nuance_en: the moment you become a fan

dict_examples.ko: 우리 오빠는 축구 팬이라서 주말마다 경기장에 가요.
dict_examples.en: My brother is a soccer fan, so he goes to the stadium every weekend.

explain_en: Several fans are 팬들. The community or culture of fans is called 팬덤 (fandom).
